D089 (2024) describes redemption rights for the 3.924% and 4.393% Notes. D086 (2025) describes redemption rights for the 4.212% and 4.319% Notes. Both disclosures describe the change of control put rights (101% of principal) and event of default acceleration clauses. D089 (2024) applies these to the 3.924% and 4.393% Notes. D087 (2025) applies them to the 4.212% and 4.319% Notes. These are distinct contractual features from the redemption provisions in D089/D086.

comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption and Change of Control Rights for Senior Notes
comparisons.peer_summary: Senior notes may be redeemed prior to maturity subject to a make-whole premium and accrued interest, and holders have the right to require repurchase at 101% of principal plus accrued interest in the event of a change in control.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom disclose standard redemption and change of control provisions for their senior notes. A key similarity is the specific repurchase price upon a change of control: both companies require paying 101% of the principal amount plus accrued interest (AMD: 'repurchase price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest'; AVGO: 'price equal to 101% of the principal amount of such notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest'). A key difference lies in the voluntary redemption mechanics: AMD uses a specific 'greater of' formula comparing present value of remaining payments or 100% of principal, whereas Broadcom explicitly references a 'specified make-whole premium determined in accordance with the indentures' in addition to accrued interest.

sentences.text: The Company may redeem some or all of the 3.924% Notes and 4.393% Notes prior to March 1, 2032 and December 1, 2051, respectively, at a price equal to the greater of the present value of the principal amount and future interest through the maturity of the 3.924% Notes or 4.393% Notes or 100% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest.

Holders have the right to require the Company to repurchase all or a portion of the 3.924% Notes or 4.393% Notes in the event that the Company undergoes a change of control as defined in the indenture, at a repurchase price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest.

We may redeem or purchase, in whole or in part, any of our senior notes prior to their respective maturities, subject to a specified make-whole premium determined in accordance with the indentures governing the respective notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest.

In the event of a change in control, note holders will have the right to require us to repurchase their notes at a price equal to 101% of the principal amount of such notes, plus accrued and unpaid interest.

peer_results.rationale: The provided Intc candidates (D134, D135) focus on issuance volumes, settlement of maturities, and general ranking of debt, but do not disclose the specific redemption pricing mechanics (e.g., present value vs. principal comparison) or the specific 101% change of control repurchase price found in AMD's disclosure, making them substantively incomparable on these specific terms.

comparisons.peer_topic: Optional Redemption Terms for Senior Unsecured Notes
comparisons.peer_summary: The company may redeem its Senior Unsecured Notes prior to maturity at the greater of 100% of principal or the present value of remaining payments, or at par between one and six months prior to maturity.
comparisons.comparison: Micron and AMD share an identical structure for their voluntary redemption pricing, specifically using the 'greater of' test between 100% of principal and the present value of remaining payments. AMD states redemption at 'the greater of the present value of the principal amount and future interest... or 100% of the principal amount' (mu_2024_8_P056_S001 parallels this with 'greater of (i) 100% of the principal amount... and (ii) the present value of the remaining scheduled payments'). However, Micron includes a distinct provision allowing redemption at par value between one and six months prior to maturity, a feature not disclosed in AMD's excerpt for these specific notes. Regarding change of control, AMD specifies the 101% repurchase price explicitly in the cited text, while Micron references the requirement in a separate covenant section.

sentences.text: The Company may redeem some or all of the 3.924% Notes and 4.393% Notes prior to March 1, 2032 and December 1, 2051, respectively, at a price equal to the greater of the present value of the principal amount and future interest through the maturity of the 3.924% Notes or 4.393% Notes or 100% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest.

We may redeem our 2026 Notes, 2027 Notes, 2028 Notes, 2029 A Notes, 2029 B Notes, 2030 Notes, 2031 Notes, 2032 Green Bonds, 2033 A Notes, 2033 B Notes, 2041 Notes, and 2051 Notes (the "Senior Unsecured Notes"), in whole or in part, at our option prior to their respective maturity dates at a redemption price equal to the greater of (i) 100% of the principal amount of the Senior Unsecured Notes to be redeemed and (ii) the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest, in each case plus accrued interest.

comparisons.peer_topic: Covenants and Change of Control Protection for Senior Unsecured Notes
comparisons.peer_summary: Senior Unsecured Notes include covenants limiting liens, sale-leaseback transactions, and mergers, with a change of control trigger requiring a purchase offer at 101% of principal plus accrued interest.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron provide change of control protection for their senior notes requiring a repurchase offer at 101% of principal plus accrued interest. AMD explicitly details this right: 'Holders have the right to require the Company to repurchase... at a repurchase price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest.' Micron similarly discloses: 'we will be required to offer to purchase such Senior Unsecured Notes at 101% of the outstanding aggregate principal amount plus accrued interest.' Unlike AMD, Micron's disclosure also explicitly links these protections to broader covenants limiting liens and mergers.

sentences.text: Holders have the right to require the Company to repurchase all or a portion of the 3.924% Notes or 4.393% Notes in the event that the Company undergoes a change of control as defined in the indenture, at a repurchase price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest.

Additionally, if a change of control triggering event, as defined in the indentures governing our Senior Unsecured Notes, occurs with respect to a series of Senior Unsecured Notes, we will be required to offer to purchase such Senior Unsecured Notes at 101% of the outstanding aggregate principal amount plus accrued interest up to the purchase date.

peer_results.rationale: The provided NVDA candidate (D001) is an introductory statement directing readers to the financial statements and contains no specific debt redemption or change of control terms comparable to AMD's detailed note provisions.
